I bought this a week ago and then they renamed the product (it was called the "Ekobrew Stainless Steel Elite Cup, Refillable Keurig K-Cups For Keurig K-Cup Brewers" when I placed the order).
Anyway, this appears to be the very same product.
I've used it about 12 times in the past week, and, overall, liked the results...until one of the perforated side panels began to peel away from the main unit.
That, in essence, is the main negative aspect of this "Ekobrew Stainless Steel Elite Cup, Refillable Keurig K-Cups For Keurig K-Cup Brewers":
it's not just one piece. So, if there is any water pressure exerted by the Keurig as it passes through the coffee grounds, the side panels can separate, as ours did. And even before it separated, some coffee grounds managed to get wedged in the crevices formed between these side panels and the main unit. And, we tried contacting Ekobrew's customer service a few days ago, anwe've received no response yet.
We'd recommend that Ekobrew make this out of one piece of metal, not 3 separate ones, as well as reply to customers when they email them.
Thanks for reading.

The kit had a main filter and 4 pre-filters.  All fit fine.  The pre-filters had to have a little pressure applied to the tabs to get them over the plastic mounting studs, but that is appropriate to keep them in place.  There were some comments from a non-physics type of person about these filters restricting the flow of air and "burning up the motor" ... cannot resist as a mechanical engineer to correct this "fakenews".  The Whirlpool Wispure 510 has a box fan arrangement.  If total flow from the filter area is blocked, the motor will spin faster due to lack of airflow resistance. This will consume approximately the same power and will generate enough turbulence that cooling will be unaffected.  Indeed, just to be sure, I tested my unit and this is what happened.  Its nice to have the electrical equipment for test power flow and remote temperature!  There are a lot of people who make a lot of sound-bite claims, but the person saying these filters will "burn up your motor" is definitely in the Alternative Facts Club.

I've used the Toddy Cold Brew system for about 2 years now. My wife and I consume iced coffee at our house like it's our life blood. So while the Toddy Cold Brew system states that the cold brew coffee will keep for something like 4 weeks, it generally makes it about 4 days in our house. I'm not kidding. All this said, we were blasting through the white replacement filters like crazy. The process of preparing the coffee is finicky and sometimes it would drain through the white filter in about 30 seconds, other times it would drain in about 30 minutes. And one clogged filter means each subsequent brew cycle will drain slowly as well. I was plunking down a bunch of money on replacement filters that I decided to give a reusable filter a shot. I haven't yet seen a quick drain with this reusable filter, but that's due to the design. The holes are small to keep out the grounds (coarse grind your coffee), and I've been subjected to lengthy drain times with the white filters, so this isn't a problem for me. I just plan ahead. Otherwise, there isn't much more in this reusable filter to gloat about. In just a couple of months this will have paid itself off and it will continue to save me money well beyond that. What more is there to love about it? Full disclosure, I was given this product at a discounted price for my fair and honest review, which you have just read. Thanks!

When I purchased the Toddy T2N Cold brew system- it came with 2 cotton filters. The filters that came with it were consistently getting clogged. Once i replaced them with the stainless steel filter, it drains much quicker, and no clogs what so ever. The stainless steel version was an extra 15 dollars- but for the taste of a good cold brew without coffee grounds- its well worth the extra couple dollars. If you are going to purchase the cold brew system- GET THE STAINLESS STEAL FILTERS!

SLIGHT VARIATION ON DIRECTIONS. There is a "burping" process that needs to happen for optimal extraction. Plug in the cork at the bottom and then ADD WATER FIRST. About a cup or two. And then take the filter and submerge it under water and wedge it into place at the bottom of the Toddy. And then add the first half of your coffee on top. Finish the rest of the instructions as they are originally.

When I did not burp I would have only half extractions even after 12 hours of drainage time. After burping it drained in less than 10 minutes. I even looked away for too long and it spilled everywhere.

I know because I accidentally ground a pound of beans too fine and I had to stir it a little to keep sludge from building up and blocking the fine holes in the filter; but when I ground the beans for a toddy (much more coarse), it has worked great ever since. Received this filter to use instead of the fiber ones that come with the Toddy cold brew system. Save a lot of money and the environment as well. Fits perfectly into the little crevis that the Toddy has and is easy to remove. Before you place this filter into the Toddy, you must put the cork in, then place about 1-2 cups of water into container. Thus ensures no trapped air is under the filter and will allow it to drain just as it should. Works better than the fiber filters.

It's nice to have something that's easier to wash than the regular filters for the Toddy, but this drains as slow as a dirty regular filter and doesn't really improve the situation.  I guess it's easier on the environment.

So here's the thing.....Does it strain coffee? Yes.  Is it more environmentally friendly than the disposable filters? Yes.  Is it easier to clean? Yes.  Does it work better? I mean....kind of?  The strainer seems like it would work just as if not more effectively than the fabric (is it fabric?) filters but it really doesn't.  Idk, maybe I had high expectations, but it just seems to have missed the mark.

It's better now that it includes a rubber gasket, but it's still not perfect.  I'd wait and see if they make a third version.  I was expecting the gasket to make it fit snugly, but it still just drops loosely into the bottom of the Toddy and you pretty much have to hope that it stays in place.  I actually thought about ordering a second one and stretching that gasket over the first, but I don't really want to have to buy a second just to get the first one to fit right.
